svg.title: TOPAK D4 — Privileged paths through the floor, and the forensic floor that survives them
svg.desc: One privileged path cannot be written as a subtraction, and it is the floor's one exception: erasure destroys authority-bearing evidence. Break-glass, which adds authority, was the second, X1, until Batch 34; X1 is retired and break-glass is an emergency seating (ADR-0052, provisional; drawn in D5). ADR-0013 writes the exception mechanism once, bounds the count (R6: one), and checks that break-glass and erasure do not compose into an unattributable effect. ADR-0028 names six classes of authority fact that no erasure may reach.
svg.text: TOPAK · D4

text.tspan: Privileged paths through the floor, and the forensic floor that survives them

svg.text: One privileged path cannot be written as a subtraction, and it is the floor's one exception: erasure destroys authority-bearing evidence. Break-glass, which adds authority, was the second, X1, until Batch 34; X1 is retired and break-glass is an emergency seating (ADR-0052, provisional; drawn in D5). ADR-0013 writes the exception mechanism once, bounds the count (R6: one), and checks that break-glass and erasure do not compose
into an unattributable effect. ADR-0028 names six classes of authority fact that no erasure may reach.

Author-ratified, and in part provisional. ADR-0013 and ADR-0028 were ratified in genesis on 2026.09.23 by the custodian alone; the first post-bootstrap quorum repays the independent reviewer that was given up. X1's retirement is in force on a record subject to redesign: ADR-0052 and the amendments that follow it (ADR-0009 A1, ADR-0013 A1, ADR-0026 A2, ADR-0041 A2) were ratified provisional on 2026.10.05 (Batch 34). If ADR-0052 is redesigned, break-glass has
no settled form until the redesign is ratified (G10 §1.2, §8; ToO §3.3).

text.tspan: X1 · Break-glass as a floor exception (ADR-0009, 09.12 acceptance) · retired
Superseded · removed by ADR-0041 A2, Batch 34

svg.text: Under a quorum of the break-glass roster, a Run seat, an agent's included, could Actuate a tool outside its allowlist and inside the issued envelope. The
approval was scoped to (seat, epoch): time-unbounded within an epoch (ADR-0052 Context; D-0052-1).
Why it went (ADR-0052 Findings): of what was asked of it, the stop is done by revocation, the addition by promotion, the record by the forensic floor; what
was left was speed. It elevated the agent; it had no bound in time; and it was the second carve-out against the floor's minimality, as ADR-0009 itself noted.
ADR-0009 A1: the path stays, its home changes. Still logged, quorum-witnessed and modeled; no longer a verified-object exception. What adds the
authority is a seating, as for every principal.

text.tspan: → D5 · Break-glass is an emergency seating

svg.text: The emergency seat kind and its alphabet; a seating prepared in advance and activated by the roster's quorum for one named person and one round; the
domain's envelope; Emergency.tla and the _A1 successors; the reference; and the exit from provisional (ADR-0052 §9; G10 item 92).

text.tspan: X2 · Erasure destroys evidence (ADR-0006): the floor's one exception

svg.text: An event: consensus-ordered, modeled in TLA+, recorded in the log it modifies. Deletion cannot be an out-of-band operator action, because that is the
capability to rewrite history.
Its authorization predicate lives in the verified object, not in a bundle: erasure operates outside the refinement lattice (09.12 acceptance).
Mechanism: deletion of sealed round topics and of plaintext-store entries; crypto-shredding rejected.
Erase of an ArchiveRecord, under an erasure quorum (context.erasureQuorum)
The erasure roster in the issued rules
NC-1 and NC-2, below, now against an emergency seating's activations
F-forensic-classes forbids Erase of any record of class F1–F6: bundles may only narrow erasure further; removing a
class is a floor relaxation (ADR-0028 §2)
A safety property that separates lawful erasure from history rewriting (ToO §4.3)
Every erasure event is itself F6, which is why demand type 5 is declined
No erasure roster is issued (ADR-0029 §5, ceremony step 5), so erasureQuorum is FALSE from epoch 0 and X2 admits
nothing. The first roster comes after bootstrap under the two-key rule (ADR-0026 §4)
Not built (G11): nothing to exercise, matching the corpus position
As linked by the reference, in the floor's emergency stage, which is genesis-provisional (ADR-0030 A3; G10 §2.2):

text.tspan: // Floor exceptions — ADR-0013 §2. Count: 1, bounded by ADR-0026 R6.

svg.text: Erasure stays a floor exception with its own roster; the seating does not touch it (ADR-0052 §7).
An activation is an F5 record (ADR-0052 §5): who approved, whom, on which seating, for which round, with the task's digest and label. Erasure does not
remove it (ADR-0013 NC-2).
Its record must outlive its round. That is a way to fail X1 did not have, since an X1 approval lasted until the epoch ended; NonComposition_A1.tla's
mutation M3 shows it, and breaks both NC-1 and NC-2 (ADR-0052 R5).
A live emergency lease leaves the erasure envelope alone: mutation M2, which lets it widen the envelope, breaks both.
Every privileged grant (promotion, break-glass, erasure) is a quorum decision on an anchor-issued roster,
bounded by the rules floor. Break-glass stays under §1 and stops being an entry under §2 (A1): its quorum seats a
person, where it used to approve a seat.
Privileged is load-bearing: ordinary Run admits are grants too, decided against a bundle, not a roster (S6-13). An
emergency seat's calls are such admits.
Issue: an environment event validated by Authentic and the rules floor; forensic class F4.
quorum → promotion (B5)
quorum → activation of an
emergency seating (D5)
quorum → X2 · none at genesis

text.tspan: Exception count, bounded by rules-floor R6

svg.text: Count 1, erasure (ADR-0013 A1 §3; ADR-0026 A2, provisional with ADR-0052). Adding an exception is a floor relaxation: an
anchor issuance and a promotion. Every carve-out works against floor minimality, which is why the count is bounded, and one
fewer is the direction it should move (ToO §3.3). Behind the records: RulesFloorBase.tla still carries R6's bound of two
and bgScope (G10 §2.1, item 90), and the reference's rules check keeps EXCEPTION_BOUND = 2 (rules.rs).
An exception is a named, versioned entry carrying its action envelope, its roster reference and its
non-composition obligations. §2's three items now describe one entry, X2.
Since ADR-0030 it is a Cedar policy inside the floor, as are the six forensic classes, so composition applies
uniformly: a bundle can narrow the exception and cannot widen it.
The floor is genesis-provisional (ADR-0030 A3): gated, pinned and enforced; ratified when the bootstrap reviewer
establishes that it is fit (ADR-0029 A4).

for A2.

text.tspan: Non-composition: NC-1 and NC-2 (ADR-0013 §4, §6, A1; ADR-0052 R5)

svg.text: Checked 2026.09.23 and proved 2026.10.02 in NonComposition.tla, which modeled X1, frozen and not edited. Restated for the seating on 2026.10.05 in its successor, NonComposition_A1.tla (d1e9113480d016bb): the activation's record is the
F5 record, the round ends, and another round is another activation with its own record.
Break-glass chained with erasure never yields an effect that is authorized, erased, and unattributable.
Erasure never removes a record in a forensic-floor class, under any composition with break-glass.

text.tspan: /\ \A r \in Rounds : <<e, r>> \in via => ActRecord(r) \in retained
NC2 == \A r \in created : r.kind \in ForensicKinds => r \in retained

svg.text: Mutations change the mechanism, never the property. M1 drops F1 from the erasure envelope's denials, so the authority trail becomes erasable. M2 lets a live emergency lease widen the erasure envelope to every class. M3, new with the seating:
an activation's record is kept only while its round is live. Under X1 there was no "after the round" in which to lose it.

spec/NonComposition_A1-results-2026.10.05.txt (fd39b1ac98780e47), TLC2 2.19, 14 rows, MaxRound = 2. Without the reachability rows NC-1 could hold because the two paths never meet. Scope: two effects, small constants; ForensicKinds = {F1,

F5, F6}, three of six classes. Proved (NonComposition_A1_proof.tla, 96 obligations, nothing assumed) and certified (57 trivial, 36 by SMT with a proof the checker accepted, 3 LS4 steps, which no checker confirms; ADR-0046 A1). A certified proof is not a
verified one, and nothing here is about the running reference. Neither successor found a fault in ADR-0052. Run by the author: evidence, not attestation.

Erasure events themselves
yes
The erasure event (unbuilt)
• All six are control-plane facts (ADR-0004) and boundary events (ADR-0020). No cognitive payload is in the floor: prompts, reasoning and review commentary remain erasable.
• No new primitive: each class is a policy-floor denial on the erasure envelope, so bundles can only narrow erasure further; removing a class or shortening the horizon is a floor relaxation (§2).
• Stop attribution is a feedback path, not just evidence: in STPA terms the Observer is a controller, not a probe (ToO §4.4).
• Same monotone shape as the policy floor, in the other direction: the policy floor caps authority, the forensic floor guarantees retention; exceptions may preserve more, never less (Context, E1).

"Immutable" lets a deployment claim conformance after erasing evidence. The archetype property: every admitted boundary event remains readable by the declared audit authority for the declared horizon.
Archetype horizon: the lifetime of the rules-epoch chain. Audit authority: the anchor plus a declared external auditor role (still to define). Shortening either is a legibility degeneracy.
The maximum projection each regime derives from.
Subtracts the record: erasure of payloads, never of F1–F6.
Six-year retention and disclosure accounting are additive and not expressed.
Subtracts the reader set: compartmentation is not erasure while the audit
authority stays a reader.
Conformant except at spill remediation.
"Hide that a record ever existed": declined. It conflicts with NC-2, since the
erasure event is F6.
A deployment needing it is outside the archetype's declared demands.
The roster is withheld by the ceremony itself (ADR-0029 §5, step 5), not by either record's status. Erasure is disabled from epoch 0: fail-closed, and it
costs nothing, since there is nothing to erase yet.
ADR-0006 therefore stands ratified with no path to exercise it until a roster is issued after bootstrap under the two-key rule, by which point ADR-0013 and
ADR-0028 have been through confirmation.

text.tspan: The forensic horizon has a seam at re-genesis

svg.text: The horizon is the lifetime of the rules-epoch chain, and re-genesis starts a new chain, which follows anchor loss or capture: the authority record lapses
exactly when it matters most.
That a successor inherits read access to its predecessor's forensic classes is a re-genesis migration obligation, open, to be settled before ADR-0028's
confirmation (ToO §4.4). ADR-0003 A1 lets a successor tell its topics apart, and settles nothing else.

text.tspan: A break-glass grant ends with its round

svg.text: R8 is withdrawn (ADR-0026 W1, 2026.10.04): a timed expiry needs trusted time (ADR-0032 §2). Item 8 is closed by the withdrawal, and item 49 decided:
an emergency seat is not coupled (G10 §7).
The round is the time box (ADR-0052 Finding 3): the activation's lease ends at the round bound R, at its ttl (at most T_persona on the local monotonic
clock, ADR-0031 A2), at an epoch increment or at a targeted revocation, and has no successor and no renewal (ADR-0013 A1).
The reference follows it since 2026.10.05: its old stand-in, an approval lapsing only at the next epoch, no longer exists there (mechanism/ register rows
